sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface detection by anti-FLAG antibody confirmed; no functional assay reported for the tagged construct in this study.
sites.rationale: L6 reports a full-length CCR7 construct with an N-terminal FLAG tag expressed in Expi293F cells and detected at the cell surface by anti-FLAG antibody, confirming the tag is accessible on the extracellular face. CCR7 has a signal peptide spanning residues 1–24 (authoritative landmark); the mature N-terminus begins at residue 25 (Q), so the tag must be placed after residue 24 to avoid co-translational cleavage. No specific residue is named in L6, but there is exactly one extracellular N-terminus (residues 25–56, 32 aa from TM1), making the junction topology-derived. Python confirmed residue 24 = C and residue 25 = Q. Full-length human CCR7 was expressed in Expi293F cells with an N-terminal FLAG tag and a C-terminal 1D4 tag; surface expression was confirmed by epitope-tag-specific antibodies (anti-FLAG detecting the extracellular N-terminus).

sources.claim: Each GPCR construct includes an N-terminal FLAG tag and a C-terminal 1D4 tag, except for four GPCRs belonging to the Frizzed (FZD) subfamily, which have an N-terminal HA (hemagglutinin) epitope tag and a C-terminal 1D4 epitope tag.

literature_notes: Six ledger lines were evaluated. L6 is the sole line grounding an extracellular tag site: it reports a full-length CCR7 construct with an N-terminal FLAG tag detected at the cell surface, placing the tag on the extracellular N-terminal domain (residues 25–56). The junction is topology-derived (insert_after_residue = 24, after signal-peptide cleavage) because L6 names no specific residue. L1 and L2 (both PMC8072677) report C-terminal EGFP and YPet fusions to full-length CCR7; L3 (PMC13436775) reports C-terminal EGFP on CCR7 isoforms; L4 and L5 (both PMC13590099) report a C-terminal FLAG-tagged CCR7 used in signaling studies. All five C-terminal tags land on the intracellular C-terminus (topology landmark: residues 330–378 are intracellular) and are therefore not surface tag sites; they are recorded in other_positions. L6 also mentions a C-terminal 1D4 tag on the same construct, which is likewise intracellular and recorded in other_positions (consolidated with L1–L5 at residue 378). No ledger line reports a tag in any extracellular loop (ECL1 120–127, ECL2 197–219, ECL3 287–302), so no internal loop sites are proposed.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal EGFP fusion to full-length CCR7 (pcDNA3-CCR7-EGFP); the C-terminus (residues 330–378) is intracellular per topology landmarks, so this tag is cytoplasmic, not a surface epitope site.
C-terminal YPet fusion via (GGGGS)3 linker to full-length CCR7 (pcDNA3-CCR7-YPet); same intracellular C-terminus as L1.
C-terminal EGFP fusions to CCR7A, CCR7B, and CCR7C isoforms expressed in HEK293 cells; C-terminus is intracellular.
C-terminal FLAG tag (via 8-aa linker) on full-length CCR7 transduced into Jurkat cells; C-terminus is intracellular despite confirmed surface expression of the receptor.
C-terminal 1D4 tag on the same full-length CCR7 construct as the N-terminal FLAG (PMC10156119); C-terminus is intracellular.
